post.caption: This famous pearl is just two brushstrokes. Johannes Vermeer painted Girl with a Pearl Earring around 1665. A bright dab sits above a soft glow that reflects her collar, and the earring has no visible hook to hold it to her ear. Experts say a real pearl this size would be astronomically expensive. Some think glass, and a 2014 theory says polished tin, but the museum's director says it is neither pearl nor glass, simply paint. Its blue headscarf is natural ultramarine, made from lapis lazuli, and in the 1600s ultramarine was reportedly worth more than gold. Before about 1995, the painting was called Girl with a Turban.
